businessProblem: Coffee Day Enterprises faces a sudden founder-death crisis in July 2019 with approximately ₹70 billion in debt, creditor confidence under severe pressure, no identified successor leadership, and a complex multi-business group structure. Diagnose root causes and recommend highest-priority action plan.

evidence.finding: Coffee Day Enterprises carrying approximately ₹70 billion (₹7,000 crore) in debt as of 2019
evidence.source: Case study sources — Emerald 2025, ResearchGate, IJAR; Coffee Day annual reports

evidence.finding: Multiple lenders and creditors had exposure to Coffee Day group entities — coordinated creditor management required
Café Coffee Day is an established large national retail café network continuing operations at decision date
Complex multi-business group structure includes non-core assets beyond the café business
evidence.source: Coffee Day Annual Report 2019, case study sources

evidence.finding: Founder V.G. Siddhartha died in late July 2019 — sudden and complete key-person loss
Founder was the central figure in creditor and investor relationships — creditor confidence immediately at risk
No publicly identified successor leadership as of decision date — governance vacuum
Café Coffee Day brand has strong recognition — preserving brand value is key to operational continuity and debt-recovery value

clientContext.companyName: Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd. / Café Coffee Day

ownerConstraintProfile.followThroughRisk: CRITICAL — founder deceased, no established successor
ownerConstraintProfile.resistanceToChange: MEDIUM — crisis may enable change if new leadership acts decisively
ownerConstraintProfile.managementCapability: UNCERTAIN — dependent on successor leadership capability
ownerConstraintProfile.keyPersonDependency: CRITICAL — founder was irreplaceable key person
ownerConstraintProfile.accountabilityWeakness: HIGH — creditor confidence undermined by sudden governance vacuum
